paper_metadata.title: Fractographic Studies of Alloys of the Ti – Al – Nb System with High Content of Niobium

evidence.quote: FRACTOGRAPHIC STUDIES OF ALLOYS OF THE Ti – Al – Nb SYSTEM WITH HIGH CONTENT OF NIOBIUM

samples.material_state: pressed, quenched from 1050°C for 1 h with air cooling

evidence.quote: Ti – 10 wt.% Al – 43.5 wt.% Nb
Ti – 10 wt.% Al – 43.5 wt.% Nb
Ti – 10 wt.% Al – 43.5 wt.% Nb

We studied fracture surfaces on specimens of two alloys, i.e., Ti – 10 wt.% Al – 43.5 wt.% Nb (Ti – 21.67 at.% Al – 27.39 at.% Nb) and Ti – 13.5 wt.% Al – 42.5 wt.% Nb (Ti – 26.65 at.% Al – 24.39 at.% Nb).

samples.material_state: pressed, quenched from 1050°C for 1 h with air cooling + annealed at 820°C for 5 h with air cooling

evidence.quote: Ti – 10 wt.% Al – 43.5 wt.% Nb
Ti – 10 wt.% Al – 43.5 wt.% Nb
Ti – 10 wt.% Al – 43.5 wt.% Nb

After heat treatment consisting of quenching from 1050°C, 1 h, air cooling + 820°C, 5 h, air cooling fracture develops by the intercrystalline mechanism with prevalence of smooth grain-boundary and virtually equiaxial facets (Fig. 1b ).
